svg.title: RPS vs Tail Latency (p95/p99) — .NET Production Mental Model (Dark)

g.text: RPS vs Tail Latency (p95/p99) — .NET Production Mental Model (Dark)
Requests arrive regardless of service response time.
Closed-workload load tests can hide the cliff.
Max Pool Size (default ~100)\n=> queue-for-connection => p99 spikes.
invalidation => thundering herd\n=> DB contention => tail explosion.
sequential calls add tails;\nparallel calls take max tail.
Gen2 pauses (50-200ms)\nimpact many in-flight requests at high RPS.
Near saturation (ρ→1): queue wait ~ ρ / (μ(1-ρ)) => p99 shoots up

"Just add instances" fails when:
- autoscaling lag
- shared DB/Redis contention
- USL β>0 (coherency) => throughput plateaus or drops
RPS ↑ => Utilization ρ ↑ => Queueing ↑ => p95/p99 cliffs
Tail latency is a *system property under load*, not a per-request attribute.
